text: A confidence interval adds an uncertainty range to an estimate. Assume twenty-five independent observations from a normal population with known standard deviation two, and a sample mean of ten. These assumptions determine the interval procedure we are about to use.
title: Idea 1

text: The mean's standard error is two divided by five, or zero point four. Multiplying by the normal cutoff, approximately one point nine six, gives a margin of zero point seven eight four. Add and subtract that margin to find the endpoints.
title: Idea 2

text: The ninety-five-percent confidence level describes repeated use of the method. Across repeated samples under these assumptions, about ninety-five percent of the resulting intervals cover the fixed population mean. It does not say that ninety-five percent of individual observations lie in this interval.
title: Idea 3

text: With the same known variability and confidence level, quadrupling sample size halves the margin. If the population standard deviation is estimated instead, use an appropriate method such as a t interval under its assumptions; do not automatically reuse the known-sigma formula.
title: Idea 4
